title: Met32 and Methionine Biosynthesis in C. albicans and Francisella novicida
summary: This cluster revolves around Met32, a gene or protein that regulates methionine biosynthesis in C. albicans. Met32 is located in the pDUP3 plasmid and has genes in both C. albicans and its met32 mutant strain. It interacts with Met4 and binds to several other genes, including JLP11, SOA1, and Seo13. C. albicans utilizes RSS and has genes for methionine biosynthesis, which is upregulated in the organism. Francisella novicida also imports GSH, a chemical related to methionine biosynthesis. The cluster also includes various other genes and chemicals involved in methionine biosynthesis and redox reactions.
